title: God's Speech to Job
hint: Who is this that darkens my counsel?
intro: After thirty-seven chapters of suffering and debate, God finally speaks—but not to explain Job's suffering. Instead, he asks Job questions about creation that reveal human limitation and God's incomprehensible greatness.

items.title: The Lord Answers from the Storm
Where Were You When the Earth Was Founded?
Who Set a Boundary for the Sea?
Have You Ever Commanded the Morning to Break Forth?
Have You Reached the Sources of the Sea?
Have You Seen the Gates of Death?
The Storehouses of Snow and Hail

footer.title: Job's Response
footer.content: God never explains why Job suffers. Instead, he shows that Job is too small to understand—and that it is enough to know that God is great enough. Job finally answered: 'My ears had heard of you, but now my eyes have seen you. Therefore I despise myself and repent in dust and ashes' (42:5-6).
